Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office receives filed documents, assigns reference numbers, routes each item to the assigned reviewer, records verification marks on the face of the document, and files the completed record in the chronological index.

2) What occurred: The actor prepared a dated document referencing a building account and a violation reference number, and submitted it through a public channel. The filing was received into the intake register, but the identity field of the sender was left unverified. The actor submitted a second document bearing a payment reference and a remittance date, requesting an update to the violation status field. The status field on the violation record was not marked as verified, and no reviewer sign-off was recorded. The actor submitted a third document bearing a correction stamp, altering the outcome code on the inspection record from a failure code to a clearance code. The correction was applied to the field without a corresponding reviewer sign-off or an audit annotation. The actor requested an index search of the case file by reference number, and the access event was logged, but the requesting identity was not matched to an authorized account.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor used a named account on the public intake portal. The actor submitted three documents through the public channel. The actor accessed the case file index by reference number. The actor's account had no reviewer role attached.

4) Indicators & artifacts: A violation record with an altered outcome code and no sign-off. A payment reference with no verified remittance record. An identity field left unverified on the intake document. An index access event with no matched authorized account. Three documents in register order with no corresponding reviewer verification marks.
